title: Runtime path instability: capacity-latch causing p95 latency spikes and follow-ups
creator: Priya Natarajan
description: During a weekend capacity surge on mixed-quant inference workloads we observed repeated p95/p99 latency spikes and sustained throughput degradation. The runtime entered a pathological state we are calling a 'capacity latch' where the scheduler consistently favored a slow fused-attention kernel variant for a subset of requests, causing microbatch pileup and eviction churn. This ticket contains the incident summary, reproduction notes, root-cause analysis, immediate mitigations applied, and prioritized action items to prevent recurrence.
impact: User-facing latency regressions for 6 hours across hosted API in us-west-2; affected customers experienced transient request timeouts and increased 95th percentile latency up to 2.8x baseline. No data loss. Estimated revenue impact: moderate for the incident window; multiple enterprise customers opened support tickets.
timeline: 2026-02-28 02:12 UTC - First uptick in p95 observed by automated SLO alerting (runtime-p95 > 250ms).
2026-02-28 02:18 UTC - Paginated on-call: initial triage showed increased queue length on a subset of workers.
2026-02-28 02:35 UTC - Tracing revealed persistent assignment to fused-attn kernel on mixed-quant models during high concurrency.
2026-02-28 03:05 UTC - Applied temporary mitigation: force-fallback policy to prefer quantized kernel variant if latency > threshold.
2026-02-28 03:30 UTC - p95 recovered to near-baseline but oscillation resumed during subsequent capacity waves.
2026-02-28 07:10 UTC - Added short-term admission control (microbatch admission cap) to limit queue build-up.
2026-02-28 08:00 UTC - Incident declared mitigated; monitoring left in elevated mode for 48h.
reproduction_steps: Deploy mixed-quant model (int8 attention weights, fp16 residuals) with typical production sequence-length distribution (~128 tokens).
Saturate a pool with concurrent short queries (high QPS spike pattern) to create microbatching pressure and KV-cache churn. Simulate ~30-60% variability in sequence length across requests.
Observe scheduler kernel scoring over time; with current heuristics, fused-attn score increases due to short-term throughput signal even though its tail latency is worse under this workload pattern.
Repeat at different host counts to show latch emerges when admission control isn't actively damping probe-induced preference.
root_cause: A combination of factors led to the capacity latch: 1) kernel scoring heuristic used a short-window throughput reward that overweighted speculative fused-attn probes, 2) hysteresis in scoring lacked an exponential decay term causing persistence of a poorer-performing kernel assignment, 3) no admission damping for microbatch admission under rapid arrivals, and 4) lack of fine-grained telemetry exposed only aggregate p95 without kernel-level correlation graphs in the console.
mitigation: Immediate mitigations included forcing a fallback to the quantized kernel variant for impacted routes, enabling a microbatch admission cap, and temporarily tightening the probe frequency for kernel candidates. These reduced tail latency but are not sustainable long-term without targeted changes to scoring and observability.
action_items: AI-1: Implement short-term decay in kernel scoring function (score_decay_half_life parameter) to avoid multi-minute stickiness. Owner: Diego Kwan. Due: 2026-03-17.

AI-2: Add a kernel-level tail-latency telemetry panel in Console (per-route kernel p50/p95/p99) and an automated alert when kernel p95 > route baseline * 1.5. Owner: Maya Chen (Observability). Due: 2026-03-15.

AI-3: Introduce probe dampening (limit speculative probe rate per-worker and per-route) and a global probe circuit-breaker that opens if probe-induced latency delta > threshold. Owner: Liam O'Connor. Due: 2026-03-22.

AI-4: Build a synthetic mixed-quant regression harness that replays production arrival patterns and validates kernel selection stability under varying sequence-length distributions. Owner: Priya Natarajan. Due: 2026-03-31.
AI-5: Create a canary rollout plan for new scoring and probe-dampening changes with detailed rollback criteria and automated metric gates. Owner: Diego Kwan + SRE. Due: 2026-03-19.

AI-6: Update admission control to add adaptive microbatch caps tied to observed KV-cache eviction rate; include a safeguard to drop non-critical low-priority requests when thresholds exceeded. Owner: Nora Alvarez. Due: 2026-03-28.
AI-7: Postmortem doc and runbook update: document 'capacity-latch' signature, triage playbook, and who to page when kernel-selection oscillation is detected. Owner: Priya Natarajan. Due: 2026-03-12.
AI-8: Add regression unit tests in scheduler CI that fail if a new scoring change increases median probe persistence in synthetic stress tests. Owner: Automation Team. Due: 2026-04-05.
AI-9: Customer communication: send summary to impacted customers and run a short Q&A for enterprise accounts. Owner: Customer Success (Emily Park). Due: 2026-03-05.
follow_up: Track metric: kernel_persistence_seconds (per-route) and aim to keep 99th percentile < 120s under normal load.
After scoring change rollout, capture 2 weeks of production data and run statistical comparison vs. baseline to ensure no regression in throughput or cost.
Schedule a cross-team post-deploy review two weeks after canary to validate SLOs and customer feedback.
